name: Republic of Angola

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Land area 1,246,700 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2, mid); high is surface area incl. inland water 1,246,700 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 39,040,039). Low allows for census uncertainty; high adds one year of growth to 2026 (~3.0%/yr).

activePersonnel.note: IISS Military Balance 2024 p.471 as quoted: 107,000 active (Army 100,000, Navy 1,000, Air 6,000). CIA Factbook 2025 ~100,000 (low); World Bank 117,000 (2020, high).

trainedReserves.note: IISS lists no organised reserve; 24-month conscription yields ex-conscripts liable to 45 (CIA Factbook). Educated guess of a callable pool.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 107,000 minus infantry P roles (25,000 + 45,000) = 37,000: navy, air force, crews, logistics, staff.

mobilizationRatio.note: Regional analogy: conscript system (20-45) and civil-war mobilization precedent, limited by equipment. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Infantry of motorised/mechanised brigades; Army ~100,000 of 107,000 (IISS 2024 as quoted). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angolan_Army)

training.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: conscripts (24 months) with civil-war veteran cadre.

count.note: Educated guess. Light infantry brigades and border units.
IISS Military Balance 2024 p.471 as quoted: T-55AM2 200 + T-62 50 + T-72M1 50 = 300, all "serviceability doubtful" (low ~1/3); PT-76 10 light tanks (high).
IISS 2024 as quoted: BMP-1 250 + MT-LB 31 + BTR-152 200 + Casspir NG2000 45 = 526 (mid); high adds BRDM-2 600 scout cars. Serviceability doubtful (low).
IISS 2024 as quoted: 2S1 9 + 2S3 4 + 2S7 12 + BM-21 70 + RM-70 40 + BM-27 3 + D-30 523 + M-46 48 + D-20 4 = 713. Low assumes half serviceable.
NAF inventory: MiG-21bis 23 + MiG-23 22 + Su-30K 12 = 57. Low ~20 flyable (Su-30K and a few MiGs).
AW109 2 + AW139 4 + Alouette III 21 + Bell 212 9 + Mi-17 65 + Mi-35 14 = 115. Low for serviceability.
IISS Military Balance 2025 pp.453-454 as quoted: HSI 32 3 + PVC-170 5 + Super Dvora Mk III 4 + Mandume 4 + Ocean Eagle 43 1 + 4 de Abril 1 = 18 (fisheries-ministry vessels excluded).

Launcher conversion at 4-6 per battery (SOURCES.md): S-75M 40, 2K12 Kub 16, S-125 12, Strela-10 10, Osa 15, Strela-1 20 = 113 launchers ~25 batteries. ZPU-4 (450+) and ZSU-23-4 guns excluded. Serviceability doubtful (low).
Educated guess. Utyos coastal launchers based at Luanda (IISS 2025 as quoted on the Navy article); number not given. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angolan_Navy)

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.25-0.5: civil-war experienced senior officers ageing; little recent large-scale operations.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: integrated MPLA/UNITA army since 1991-2002.

logistics.note: Anchor 8-9: Il-76/An-12 airlift, Lobito Corridor railway.

isr.note: Anchor 9 minus: C-295 MSA maritime patrol, AngoSat-2.

air.note: Anchor 9 minus: Su-30K plus obsolete MiGs.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 273,769,552,092 2011 int$ / population 39,040,039 = 7,013. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 341,998,191,246 x 0.8005 = 273,769,552,092 2011 int$. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 1.40% of GDP in 2025.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction (and mining/oil where present) 27.1% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). +/-2 points.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.05 -> 0.34. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/AGO/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 51.95% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.79 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.77-0.80). Mid 1 - 0.519/0.79 = 0.34. Low: a x 1.2 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.77 = 0.19. High: s 0.80 = 0.35. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 79% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Net food importer despite large arable potential. Not from FAO balance sheets.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 19,322,247 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share aged 15-19 10.838% / 5 = 418,824. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10%.

roadKm.note: Road list (2020): 76,000 km total (high), 13,680 km paved (mid).

railKm.note: CIA Factbook: 2,761 km (2022); no World Bank value. Low allows for disused track. Three unconnected lines from Luanda, Lobito (Benguela railway, Lobito Corridor) and Namibe.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 21 ports, none large/medium, 8 small (Luanda, Lobito, Namibe, Cabinda + oil terminals). Mid counts Luanda, Lobito, Namibe.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. CIA Factbook: 64 ships under the Angolan flag (2023); not in the DWT list. (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/africa/ao.json)

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Truck sustainment over poor roads; Soviet-pattern logistics.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Few draft animals outside the southern cattle zone (not from FAO data).

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: vast territory, familiar terrain, civil-war experience, population support.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data, 2026 order of battle. Ground and naval counts are IISS Military Balance 2024/2025 figures as quoted (sfn page cites) on the Wikipedia Angolan Army equipment list and Angolan Navy article; IISS itself flags most army equipment as "serviceability doubtful", so lows are set at about a third to a half. Population convention: everything inside ne:AGO including Cabinda. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). 10,000 paramilitary (Rapid Reaction Police) excluded.
